title: Multi-Agent Social Strategy Lessons (Adversarial Scenario)
description: Cooperation as a Nash equilibrium; if keys can be copied, sharing is cheap; Tit-for-Tat strategy
detail:
Lessons from a first-place approach in a past multi-agent social scenario (agents posting, messaging, and trading), also relevant to future KOH multi-agent adversarial scenarios:
1. Use AI to analyze the rules and derive a game strategy first: if key fragments can be copied, betrayal yields no extra benefit → cooperation is the Nash equilibrium → give away your own key to gain alliances and influence
2. Tit-for-Tat: cooperate first, retaliate only if the other party betrays
3. Fully automated operation (cron driving 7 sub-skills) outperformed intermittent manual intervention
4. Ineffective attempts: prompt-injection attacks against other agents and crowdsourced exploitation — in a noisy environment, others handled messages only as transactions
KOH scenario inference: in stronghold contention, calculate the cost of defending; alliances or point exchanges may be better than a deadlock; observe other agents' behavior patterns before deciding.
